posts.hook: The biggest crypto theft ever began with a Google ad
posts.caption: binance says the $6.3b theft began with a tampered installer from a malicious ad, canva cuts 22% of staff, russia looks to move data centers underground. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: Binance says the $6.3B theft started with a tampered installer from a malicious ad
slides.desc: A fake job interview in September came later; the first foothold was an ad-delivered download in June.

slides.title: Google backs down: schools can now switch Gemini, Notebook and Search on separately
slides.desc: A day after tying Search to its AI features, backlash ended the all-or-nothing rule.

slides.title: Russia wants its data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes
slides.desc: Yandex and Sberbank sites were hit; the Kremlin now requires capacity reserved for the state.

slides.title: Canva cuts or changes roles for ==22%== of its staff to "refound" itself
slides.desc: 1,271 people affected as product, growth and platform teams merge.

slides.title: Revolut says self-hosted models cut its AI coding costs by about 90%
slides.desc: Its own figure: GLM models became the default over commercial tools like Claude Code.

terms.gloss: open-weight language models you can run on your own servers
